memory_update.text: KYOCY mapped to AI-server MLCC/specialty ceramic capacitor node as an underfollowed second-order hypothesis; key survival test is direct KYOCERA AVX evidence in AI accelerator boards, server power, networking, or hyperscaler-qualified MLCC supply chains.

MTRN mapped to upstream electronic-ceramic/dielectric-powder node as a weak underfollowed hypothesis; key survival test is proof of commercial BaTiO3 or comparable high-end MLCC powder products and capacitor-maker customers.
CBT mapped to MLCC dielectric-powder node only as speculative shadow; should be removed unless current retained barium-titanate/electronic-ceramics assets or successor economics are documented.
Need primary-source validation for all three tickers: annual reports, product catalogs, technical datasheets, patents, customer/design-win references, distributor lead times, and earnings commentary.

Need market-pricing checks for KYOCY, MTRN, and CBT: market cap, analyst coverage, AI/MLCC keyword frequency in filings and calls, relative performance since AI-server MLCC narrative surfaced, and whether any perceived hidden exposure is already priced.

summary: Mapped three public tickers from the AI-server MLCC / upstream dielectric-powder candidate chunk. Kyocera is the strongest relationship in this chunk, but still a hypothesis because evidence provided only supports broad MLCC-maker benefit and not confirmed AI accelerator/server socket exposure for KYOCERA AVX. Materion remains a weaker underfollowed materials hypothesis requiring product/customer proof that it sells BaTiO3 or related electronic-ceramic powders into high-end MLCC supply chains. Cabot is downgraded to speculative shadow because current evidence is stale/absent for any retained barium-titanate ceramic-materials business. No buy/sell recommendation is made.
